{{- /* A page-relative URL (`../on-drill/`, `./quickstart/`, `insightview/`, `shot.png`) made root-relative against the page it is written on, in the form relref and .RelPermalink use, so a render hook or shortcode then treats it like any other root-relative URL. Same rule as the Markdown copy (page-markdown.html): `#fragment` and `?query` are kept, and so is a trailing slash; `..` and `.` keep the slash too, as a browser would resolve them. Why: every page is a directory (…/on-drill/), and a relative link resolves against the URL the browser loaded. www.gooddata.ai also serves …/on-drill without the slash (the proxy in front of Netlify drops its slash redirect), and there `../drillable-items/` lands one level too high: opened as …/latest, every link on the docs home was a 404. Resolved at build time, the link works either way. Anything else (a scheme, `//host`, root-relative `/…`, `#anchor`, `?query`, empty) is returned as written. So is a shortcode's output (a relref in a link's destination): a render hook runs before the shortcode is expanded and sees Hugo's placeholder (HAHAHUGOSHORTCODE-…), which is replaced by the root-relative link afterwards. Expects dict "page" and "url"; returns the URL. */ -}} {{- $url := .url -}} {{- if and $url (not (findRE `^(?:[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*:|//|/|#|\?)` $url)) (not (strings.Contains $url "HUGOSHORTCODE")) -}} {{- $path := $url -}} {{- $rest := "" -}} {{- with findRE `[?#].*$` $url 1 -}} {{- $rest = index . 0 -}} {{- $path = strings.TrimSuffix $rest $url -}} {{- end -}} {{- $dir := or (hasSuffix $path "/") (eq $path ".") (eq $path "..") (hasSuffix $path "/.") (hasSuffix $path "/..") -}} {{- $joined := path.Clean (path.Join .page.RelPermalink $path) -}} {{- if and $dir (ne $joined "/") -}}{{- $joined = printf "%s/" $joined -}}{{- end -}} {{- $url = printf "%s%s" $joined $rest -}} {{- end -}} {{- return $url -}}
